bodyHtml:
A decision guide to Open-Kritt: what it is for, when it fits, how to start, and which compatibility or maintenance details deserve a closer look.

Quick verdict

Orchestrate AI agents to find real vulnerabilities in code.

Shortlist Open-Kritt only if its documented purpose matches your use case; the source signals below are context, not an endorsement.

Best fit — and when to skip it

Open-Kritt is most relevant to developers working with JavaScript. Its source topics point to agent, agents, ai, bug bounty. It belongs on a shortlist when that stated purpose matches a concrete requirement.

Skip or postpone it when the documented runtime, license, dependency footprint, or maintenance model conflicts with your project. Popularity alone is not a reason to migrate.

Setup and first checks

Read the README, recent releases, issue tracker, security policy, and license before cloning Open-Kritt. Start in a disposable environment that matches your runtime and deployment constraints.

Maintenance and risk signals

The collected source record shows 347 GitHub stars, 75 forks, 18 open issues, and last source push 2026-07-22.

The source reports the AGPL-3.0 license.

Stars, forks, and issue counts show repository activity or attention; they do not prove quality, security, or suitability.

Bottom line

Open-Kritt is worth a closer look when its stated purpose and ecosystem fit your project. Compare it with related tools, verify the current documentation, and test the smallest realistic use case before committing.

Start with the official repository

git clone https://github.com/Kritt-ai/open-kritt

Read the repository documentation, recent releases, issue tracker, security policy, and license before using the project. Try it in a disposable or non-production environment first.
